failure_semantics.admitted: COMMIT returned success, writer closed, a fresh read-only connection reconstructed one exact row, the canonical CBOR bytes round-tripped, and all checked columns rejoined the independently decoded JSON and CBOR semantics.
failure_semantics.committed_unverified: COMMIT returned success but close, reopen, schema, row, byte, or semantic reconstruction did not complete exactly. The handoff is terminal and no retry is permitted.
failure_semantics.precommit_rejected: COMMIT was not entered, rollback and close completed, and no admitted row exists. The handoff is poisoned and no retry is permitted.
failure_semantics.transaction_outcome_unknown: COMMIT was entered but did not return success, or rollback/close could not establish the precommit state. The handoff is terminal and no retry is permitted. Inspection is evidence-only.
failure_semantics.unavailable: A competing call observes IN_PROGRESS; a later call observes ALREADY_CONSUMED, COMMIT_REQUIRES_INSPECTION, EXPIRED, or POISONED according to the retained process-local state.

filesystem_admission.directory_inventory: descriptor-rooted openat-dot plus fdopendir/readdir joined to the held directory vnode
filesystem_admission.failure_retention: Rejected, unknown, and committed-unverified outcomes do not delete or reinterpret offending entries; a retained unexpected sidecar or inventory entry is evidence of non-admission.

nonclaims: This freeze authorizes implementation and bounded local tests only; it does not enter or complete H4.
It does not create a production storage-path capability, production H3 mint, live H3 run, VM/process action, graph, Merkle root, release projection, Gate-E promotion, or authority bit.
SQLite is a durable container and checked projection, not semantic, transition, execution, or scientific authority.

No owner anchor, epoch, source identity, envelope identity, run identifier, timestamp, digest, filesystem path, or diagnostic payload is serialized or stored in SQLite, its transient rollback journal, or the success receipt.

The D2 lease closes process-local replay of ordinary handoff copies. Restart-spanning replay, same-user host mutation resistance, rollback resistance, authenticity, WAL/crash recovery, disk-full behavior, and partial physical-write behavior remain separate D2b or later evidence obligations.
SQLite still opens the database by its admitted named path rather than a held-descriptor custom VFS. Ancestor mutation and same-user ABA inside the named-open gap are not excluded.

A rollback journal can transiently contain page copies only while the owned writer transaction may exist. No secure erase, backup exclusion, snapshot exclusion, or at-rest cryptographic protection is claimed.
The fresh read-only reopen is in the same process. It is not crash, power-loss, restart-adoption, disk-full, SQLITE_IOERR, or partial-physical-write evidence.
A successful fixture transaction does not convert the structural H3 fixture into verified-live product provenance.

sqlite.schema_sql: CREATE TABLE h4_receipts(singleton INTEGER PRIMARY KEY CHECK(singleton=1),semantic_schema TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(semantic_schema='com.ergentics.provenance.hypervisor.h4.canonical-receipt.v1'),claim_state TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(claim_state='OBSERVED_NONPASS'),predicate_count INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(predicate_count>0 AND predicate_count<=4096),authority_vector TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(authority_vector='00000000'),canonical_cbor BLOB NOT NULL CHECK(length(canonical_cbor)>0 AND length(canonical_cbor)<=158)) STRICT, WITHOUT ROWID
sqlite.transaction: one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction creates the frozen schema, sets user_version/application_id, inserts exactly one row, reads it back, and COMMITs

store_grant.admission_deadline: inclusive valid-through tick checked at grant claim and immediately before COMMIT
store_grant.owner_join: private object-identity join to the D1 owner epoch anchor

success_receipt.construction: fileprivate and reachable only after exact committed close/reopen reconstruction
success_receipt.variable_metadata: absent; no predicate count or CBOR byte count is exposed

test_schedule: zero-argument coordinator success and exact close/reopen reconstruction
ordinary handoff copies share one persistence lease
a separate owner-joined store grant has an inclusive deadline, one winner, terminal replay, and a fixed retention rule
sequential and concurrent calls have exactly one admitted winner
expiry before claim poisons without SQLite transaction
pre-BEGIN, post-BEGIN, post-schema, and post-insert injected failures roll back and never admit a row
entered-COMMIT and post-COMMIT schedules produce named terminal unknown or committed-unverified states and never retry
schema/application version, extra schema object/column, row cardinality, storage-class attempt, byte, and checked-column mismatch never produce an admitted receipt

existing database, pre-open journal, live-transaction journal mode/hard-link/symlink-shaped metadata fault injection through the production validator, post-COMMIT journal, parent alias/mode, database mode/vnode replacement/nlink, unknown entry, oversized file, and non-page-aligned initialized file reject
explicit close and read-only reopen failures after COMMIT remain committed-unverified
the exact canonical JSON stream and diagnostic, owner, epoch, root, path, and SQL-detail canaries are absent from the database, receipt, errors, and reflection
an external static application-binary audit must show that EPR_H4_PRIVACY_TESTS, test store/path/fault seams, and arbitrary raw reopened-stream entry points are absent
